reasons.A: Long, subordinate-heavy sentences, explanatory essay stance and American 'faucet' diction are far from the passage's clipped, plain, first-person British narration.
reasons.B: Keeps the passage's past-tense first-person account in short declaratives and fragments with plain British diction and dry asides, though its imperative instruction paragraphs and 'It was not nothing' push slightly towards a manual and towards imitation.
reasons.C: Short sentences and fragments fit, but the shift to present tense and a procedural 'here is the order I work in' stance, plus piled-on fragments like 'Not good.' and 'Firmly.', read more like caricature than the passage's even narrative.
